newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPECTRE OF LAST-MATCH DISASTER HANGS OVER REAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPECTRE OF LAST-MATCH DISASTER HANGS OVER REAL.

text.p: The spectre of last-match disasters in successive seasons is hanging over Real Madrid's fans after defeat at Athletic Bilbao left their side just two points clear of Barcelona with three games to play.
Real lost to Tenerife and handed the championship to their arch-rivals after squandering similar leads in both 1992 and 1993.
Spanish newspapers on Monday were quick to draw comparison with one of the blackest pages in the club's history.
"Real Madrid relive the Tenerife syndrome," read a headline in the El Pais.
Despite having seen a nine-point advantage slip through their hands, the Real players have downplayed their problems.
"This league is not going to escape us," said Raul Gonzalez.
Suspensions meant that the teenage international was the only first-choice striker playing for Real in Sunday's game.
Real's other main attacking weapon, Brazilian set-piece ace Roberto Carlos, will miss the rest of the season because of international duty.
But Real will be boosted by the return of forwards Davor Suker and Predrag Mijtovic in next weekend's home game against Extremadura.
Extremadura desperately need the points and may prove a hard nut to crack after forcing a draw out of Atletico Madrid.
Atletico will be Real's next opponents and they end the season at Celta Vigo, a side drifting in mid-table with little to play for.
But Barcelona's run in is not noticeably easier.

Bobby Robson's men must travel to Hercules, a team all but condemned to relegation, before hosting high-flying Real Betis who appear to be concentrating on their June 28 Spanish Cup final date against Barcelona.
To be in a position to take what would be a unique Cup, Cupwinners' Cup and league treble, Barcelona will almost certainly have to win a difficult away match at Rayo Vallecano.
Rayo became the first side to beat Real Madrid earlier in the season and look set to be fighting to avoid relegation right to the last match.
And for at least the final two games, Barcelona will be missing striker Ronaldo. The young Brazilian will be playing a series of games for his national side.
